summary: Describes the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP), a reliable transport protocol that can carry multiple independent message streams in one connection. It was later replaced by RFC 4960.

eli5.summary: SCTP is like TCP but can carry several separate conversations at once, so a delay in one does not block the others.

questions: how does the sctp four-way handshake work
how is sctp different from tcp
subtitle: A message-oriented, multi-stream, multi-homed transport protocol that began as a way to carry telephone signaling over IP.

tldr.problem: TCP forces strict ordering of all data, has no message boundaries, does not handle multi-homed hosts well and is vulnerable to SYN attacks, all of which hurt applications such as PSTN signaling transport.
tldr.mechanism: SCTP sets up an association with a four-way cookie handshake, carries user messages as chunks on independent streams, acknowledges data by TSN with selective acks, and can use several IP addresses at each end.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2960 is the original SCTP specification and has been replaced by RFC 4960, with RFC 3309 as an update.

today: RFC 2960 is obsoleted by RFC 4960 and was updated by RFC 3309. For the current SCTP specification, read RFC 4960.

sections.title: Why SCTP Exists
sections.content:
The Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) is a reliable transport protocol that runs on top of a connectionless network such as IP. It was designed to transport PSTN signaling messages over IP networks but can serve broader applications.

The RFC lists four TCP limits that applications were working around, often by building their own reliability over UDP:

  • TCP gives reliable and strictly ordered delivery, and some applications need reliability without ordering or with only partial ordering. Head-of-line blocking then causes unnecessary delay.
  • TCP is a byte stream, so applications must add their own record marking and use the push facility.
  • TCP sockets are a poor fit for highly available data transfer on multi-homed hosts.
  • TCP is relatively vulnerable to denial of service attacks such as SYN attacks.

SCTP offers acknowledged, error-free, non-duplicated transfer, fragmentation to fit the path MTU, sequenced delivery within multiple streams with an option for order-of-arrival delivery, optional bundling of messages and fault tolerance through multi-homing.
sections.eli5: Regular TCP is a single-file line where everyone waits for the slowest person. SCTP lets several lines move at once and keeps whole letters together instead of one long strip of words.

sections.title: Packets, Chunks and Associations
sections.content:
An SCTP association is a relationship between two endpoints. Unlike a TCP connection, each endpoint can offer a list of transport addresses (several IP addresses plus one SCTP port) and the association covers all source and destination combinations. Two endpoints must not have more than one association between them at a time.

An SCTP packet is a common header followed by one or more chunks. The common header holds the source and destination port numbers, a 32-bit Verification Tag and a 32-bit checksum. Each chunk has a type, flags, a length and a value. INIT, INIT ACK and SHUTDOWN COMPLETE chunks must not be bundled with any other chunk.

A DATA chunk carries a TSN, a Stream Identifier, a Stream Sequence Number and a Payload Protocol Identifier, followed by the user data, padded to a 4-byte boundary. Its flags are U (unordered), B (beginning fragment) and E (ending fragment): both B and E set means an unfragmented message. Chunk types defined here include DATA (0), INIT (1), INIT ACK (2), SACK (3), HEARTBEAT (4), HEARTBEAT ACK (5), ABORT (6), SHUTDOWN (7), SHUTDOWN ACK (8), ERROR (9), COOKIE ECHO (10), COOKIE ACK (11) and SHUTDOWN COMPLETE (14).
sections.eli5: A packet is an envelope with a label on the front and several small notes inside. Each note says what kind of note it is, so one envelope can hold a few messages at once.

sections.title: The Four-Way Handshake and Shutdown
sections.content:
SCTP starts an association with a four-way handshake built around a state cookie. Endpoint A sends INIT with its Verification Tag. Endpoint Z answers with INIT ACK, which carries Z's own tag and a State Cookie. A returns the cookie in COOKIE ECHO, and Z replies with COOKIE ACK. The last two legs may carry user data.

After sending the INIT ACK, Z must not allocate resources or keep state for the new association, so a flood of INITs cannot exhaust it. The cookie contains the information needed to rebuild the state plus a MAC computed with a secret key, a timestamp and a lifespan. When a COOKIE ECHO arrives, the receiver recomputes the MAC, silently discards the packet if it fails, and sends a Stale Cookie error if the cookie has expired.

Each end chooses the number of outbound streams it wants and the maximum inbound streams it will accept, and the two sides reconcile them.

Closing can be graceful (SHUTDOWN, SHUTDOWN ACK, SHUTDOWN COMPLETE) or abrupt (ABORT). SCTP has no half-open state: once either side shuts down, both sides stop accepting new data from their users and deliver only what is already queued.
sections.eli5: The first greeting costs the host nothing. The host hands you a sealed ticket and only sets up your seat after you bring the ticket back, so pranksters who never return the ticket cannot fill the room.

sections.title: Streams, Ordering and Acknowledgement
sections.content:
A stream is a one-way logical channel inside which messages are delivered in order. The receiver holds back later messages in a stream that is waiting for a missing one, but other streams keep delivering. A message sent with the U flag set skips ordering and is delivered as soon as it is reassembled.

Reliability and ordering are kept separate. Every DATA chunk gets a 32-bit Transmission Sequence Number (TSN), independent of the 16-bit Stream Sequence Number within the stream. The receiver acknowledges every TSN it gets with a SACK chunk, even when there are gaps, and sends a SACK with Gap Ack Blocks right away when it detects a gap. Fragments of one message use strictly sequential TSNs and the same stream sequence number.

A sender may fragment messages to fit the path MTU, and a receiver must support reassembly. The common header carries a 32-bit Adler-32 checksum over the whole packet, and a packet that fails it is silently discarded.
sections.eli5: Every package gets a ticket number so lost ones can be spotted. Packages also belong to a lane, and a stuck package only holds up its own lane.

sections.title: Congestion Control and Path Management
sections.content:
SCTP uses slow start and congestion avoidance based on the TCP algorithms of RFC 2581, applied to the whole association rather than to each stream. A sender must not be more aggressive than the algorithms allow. One rwnd is kept per association, while cwnd, ssthresh and partial_bytes_acked are kept for each destination address of a multi-homed peer.

Each endpoint picks a primary path, used by default. Replies such as SACK normally go to the address the triggering chunk came from. Retransmissions should go to a different active address. Failure detection uses counters: if consecutive retransmissions exceed Association.Max.Retrans, the peer is unreachable and the association closes. If a destination address exceeds Path.Max.Retrans, it is marked inactive and the user is notified.

On idle addresses, SCTP sends periodic HEARTBEAT chunks to check reachability, and the peer answers with HEARTBEAT ACK.

The RFC recommends RTO.Initial of 3 seconds, RTO.Min of 1 second, RTO.Max of 60 seconds, Valid.Cookie.Life of 60 seconds, Association.Max.Retrans of 10 attempts, Path.Max.Retrans of 5 attempts, Max.Init.Retransmits of 8 attempts and HB.interval of 30 seconds.
sections.eli5: SCTP slows down when the road is jammed, just as TCP does. If one road to a friend's house is blocked, it quietly tries another road and uses little check-in calls to see which roads still work.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The stated security objectives are availability of reliable, timely transport and integrity of the user-to-user information. The RFC says SCTP's design resists flooding through the four-way handshake, the cookie that delays committing resources, and the Verification Tag that stops extraneous packets entering an established association. Blind masquerade is hard because the INIT ACK with the cookie goes back to the address that sent the INIT.

For stronger integrity, the IP Authentication Header SHOULD be used. For confidentiality, user data can be encrypted by the application or the IP Encapsulating Security Payload used, with ISAKMP and IKE for key management. The RFC also warns that the Host Name feature in INIT could be abused to flood a DNS server, and suggests checking that the resolved addresses include the INIT's source address. It advises limiting the number of associations per adjoining node.
sections.eli5: The cookie trick and the secret tag make it hard for strangers to barge in or fake being someone else. For truly secret mail you add a locked box around it.

fields.name: Destination Port Number
fields.desc: Used to deliver the packet to the right endpoint or application.

fields.name: Verification Tag
fields.desc: Lets the receiver validate that the packet belongs to the current association.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: Adler-32 checksum of the whole packet.

messages.label: INIT ACK
messages.note: Carries Z's tag and a State Cookie; Z keeps no state.

messages.label: COOKIE ECHO
messages.note: Returns the cookie; may be bundled with DATA.

transitions.label: rcv INIT ACK: send COOKIE ECHO
rcv valid COOKIE ECHO: send COOKIE ACK
rcv SHUTDOWN ACK: send SHUTDOWN COMPLETE
no outstanding data: send SHUTDOWN ACK
